Return to the journey
# Refinement 9 — Implementation and verification report

Date: 11 November 2026. Existing project retained; no rebuild.

## Mobile journey input
The journey pointer handlers were attached only to the WebGL canvas. The lower chapter text sits above that canvas and receives the initial touch, so a swipe beginning there never reached the journey handler. A blanket canvas touch-action restriction also did not express ownership between journey navigation and active viewers.

The journey now has a document-level capture handler restricted to journey mode and usable content. It includes chapter headings/body text, waits for a 9-pixel movement threshold, rejects predominantly horizontal movements, and suppresses accidental clicks after a drag. It excludes navigation, dialogs, globe cards, Rosary tools and scrollable Luminous detail. Pointer capture begins only after a recognized journey drag and is released on completion, cancellation, resize and mode changes. Active Earth/Rosary/artifact viewers retain their own canvas handlers. Native information scrollers retain vertical touch scrolling. Touch cancellation applies only to an owned journey gesture, not globally. Decorative overlays ignore pointer input.

## Captions and globe cards
Removed the public “Resized to maximum 960 pixels and JPEG-optimized…” processing note and the corresponding display-caption path. All photograph captions use the destination's proper name; descriptive alternative text remains separate. Source and license records remain in Sources & Credits, linked from each photo. Historical dates, place associations, prayer intentions and source URLs are retained. Credit headings use proper names; history entries sharing shrine photographs have their own valid credit anchors.

Cards use consistent image presentation, serif caption typography, spacing and readable secondary text. The main card area remains one scroller with reachable previous/next controls. Intentions receive additional spacing and contrast. Short screens constrain optional detail areas; full chapter text remains available through the chapter button.

## Crucifix
Replaced the former oval/cylinder figure with a continuous profiled torso and a sculpted face incorporating nose, closed eyes, brow, cheek and mouth relief. Curved tapered arms/legs, separate fingers/toes, overlapped feet, flowing hair, beard, a woven thorn crown and a folded modest loincloth add depth. Slight head inclination and restrained metal/patina finishes distinguish the corpus from the cross. Existing beveled cross, INRI plaque/inscription, overall scale and centerpiece remain intact. Geometry is consolidated by finish into three meshes, 25,190 triangles. No gore or external heavyweight model was added.

An offline render was used to review proportions and depth. This is not a certification of in-browser WebGL lighting or normal-distance readability on a phone.

## The Rosary Today
Uses the exact supplied Golden Light at the Grotto PNG (1448 × 1086), replacing the previous image reference. Scene geometry follows the photograph's actual aspect ratio. Full-image fallback presentation uses contain sizing and a very narrow edge blend. The elderly woman on the left, all other people, statue, flowers and candles remain in the composition. Existing chapter title, description and button remain website elements.

## Verification results and limits
- Passed all existing automated suites: scene construction/update, timeline continuity, marker focus/picking and backside rejection, shrine datasets and coordinates, 59-bead topology, prayer sequence, Rosary mouse rotation/panning and simulated two-pointer zoom/pan.
- Passed added input tests for lower chapter text, gesture threshold, reverse navigation, exclusion of other modes and native panels, and pointer capture release.
- Passed geometry checks: finite positions/normals, three corpus meshes, triangle budget, retained INRI inscription.
- Passed caption checks: no processing or photographic-composition caption path, proper names, source targets for every photographed destination, supplied image present.
- Running Chromium preview: lower chapter-text mouse drag advanced the journey; detail/menu scrolling worked independently. Portrait 390 × 844 and landscape 844 × 390 previews showed the full grotto group. These were responsive previews, not real touch-device tests.
- Calculated grotto scene bounds fit 1366 × 900 desktop, 390 × 844 portrait and 844 × 390 landscape viewports.
- Offline sculpture rendering reviewed; actual WebGL browser rendering was unavailable.

**Not certified:** real-phone portrait/landscape swipes, native pinch zoom and panning, GPU appearance/performance, final mobile overlay interactions, and full live music/keyboard/end-navigation regression. This environment reports WebGL unavailable and its organization policy blocks browser device tools. No policy bypass was attempted. The requested real-phone/touch-capable acceptance testing remains outstanding; automated pointer simulation and responsive previews do not replace it.

Historical Development and 30 Shrines Around the World datasets, celestial background, music implementation and final navigation remain in the project. Existing “30 Shrines” presentation includes 32 schedule entries (including Vatican opening/closing events); that established dataset was preserved.
